title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-03-02
source: Bertha Remaster of the Multi-Track source.

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a raw 1969 show opening with a soaring Dark Star and epic jams, highlighted by The Eleven and a scorching Cryptical > Other One sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers a clear‑ish soundboard feed that lets the band’s 1969 fire shine through – from the opening Dark Star to the relentless jam on The Eleven and the urgent Cryptical > Other One stretch. Reviewers rave about the psychedelic keyboard work, Garcia’s “nailed” lead on Death Don't Have No Mercy, and Phil Lesh’s ever‑present bass backbone, while noting only a brief cut at the end of Goodnight.

ai_rating.rationale: One highly enthusiastic 5‑star review emphasizes an outstanding performance and generally good soundboard quality; limited data keeps confidence low.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Overall clear enough to enjoy the psychedelic keyboards and heavy jams; a brief cut on the Goodnight finale and occasional feedback in the space segment are the only noted issues.

standout_songs: Death Don't Have No Mercy (Garcia nailed)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert launches with a monster Dark Star that segues into St. Stephen, The Eleven and Lovelight, then a concise second‑set opener followed by high‑energy Cryptical > Other One, powerful ballads, extended jams and a sweet Goodnight ending.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s lead on 'Death Don't' is described as nailed; his heavy presence drives the long jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is noted as ever‑present, providing a solid bass backbone throughout the improvisations.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keyboard work on Dark Star is called very psychedelic with classical fugue elements, likely Tom Constanten’s contribution.
band_member_comments.Drums: Heavy drumming is mentioned during jam sections; no specific complaints about timing or mix.
